candidate.answerReason: The half-plane condition gives ∠FDE=160°. Since DE=DF, the base angle ∠DFE is 10°, making its adjacent supplementary angle ∠AFE equal to 170°.

methods.label: Equal base angles
methods.explanation:
The equality \(DE=DF\) makes \(\triangle DEF\) isosceles, so first find its angle at \(D\). Since \(ABCD\) is a square and \(F\) lies on \(AD\), we have \(\angle CDF=90^\circ\). The half-plane condition places \(DE\) across line \(CD\) from \(DF\), so the angles around \(D\) give
\[
\angle FDE=360^\circ-90^\circ-110^\circ=160^\circ.
\]
The equal sides \(DE\) and \(DF\) have equal opposite angles. Thus
\[
\angle DFE=\angle DEF
=\frac{180^\circ-160^\circ}{2}=10^\circ.
\]
As shown, \(F\) is between \(A\) and \(D\), so rays \(FA\) and \(FD\) are opposite. Therefore
\[
\angle AFE=180^\circ-10^\circ=170^\circ,
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
